Data

The unit of analysis for breaches is a closed-mouth day, WY2019 to WY2026: every day the mouth was closed at the start of the day, ending with the breach day itself. The outcome is whether the berm breached that day. All inputs are known by the end of that day, as they would be in a forecast. Breach days are dated by when the slough began to drain in the sub-daily water-level record, not the day CCBER logged the open mouth (src/breach_timing.py): three breaches that drained overnight after a rain day, or with no logger record and rain only the day before, count on that rain day.

Input Meaning
rain_in rain that day (in, Coal Oil Point gauge scale)
rain_3d rain over the last 3 days
api antecedent precipitation index (daily decay 0.9): how wet the watershed already is
rain_wy rain since October 1
log_dc log of days since the mouth closed (berm age)
stage slough level (ft NAVD88): yesterday’s measured level rolled forward with today’s rain
tide_max highest predicted tide that day (ft NAVD88)
surge largest observed-minus-predicted ocean level that day (ft): storm surge
hs_max largest significant wave height at the Harvest buoy (m)
wave30 30-day mean wave power (H²T)

Part 1. Which inputs predict a breach?

Before fitting: sample size, collinearity, separation

Events per variable. With only 14 breaches, the usual guidance for logistic regression (5 to 10 events per estimated coefficient) supports about 2 to 3 predictors. Larger models overfit. So the search below caps models at 4 predictors and ranks them by leave-one-water-year-out cross-validation rather than in-sample fit.

One input at a time

Code 
def fit_logit(df, cols):
    Xm = sm.add_constant((df[cols] - df[cols].mean()) / df[cols].std())
    try:
        return sm.Logit(df.breach.values, Xm).fit(disp=0, maxiter=200)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:  # near-separable: a vanishingly small ridge keeps it finite
        return sm.Logit(df.breach.values, Xm).fit_regularized(alpha=1e-4, disp=0, maxiter=500)

null = sm.Logit(y, np.ones((n_days, 1))).fit(disp=0)
rows = []
for c in CANDS:
    m = fit_logit(risk, [c])
    lr = 2 * (m.llf - null.llf)
    rows.append(dict(input=c, coef_per_SD=m.params[c], odds_ratio_per_SD=np.exp(m.params[c]),
                     LR_chi2=lr, p_value=stats.chi2.sf(lr, 1), AUC=roc_auc_score(y, m.predict())))
uni = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("LR_chi2", ascending=False)
uni.round({"coef_per_SD": 2, "odds_ratio_per_SD": 2, "LR_chi2": 1, "p_value": 4, "AUC": 3})

Every combination of up to four inputs

Each model is fit eight times, leaving out one water year each time and predicting it. Scores use only those held-out predictions. A breach counts as caught when the predicted chance reaches 50% on the breach day or the day before; a false-alarm day is a day at 50% or more that is more than 2 days from any breach.

Code 
years = risk.water_year.values
breach_days = d.index[d.breach == 1]
near = np.zeros(n_days, bool)
for b in breach_days:
    near |= (risk.index >= b - pd.Timedelta(days=2)) & (risk.index <= b + pd.Timedelta(days=2))
ev_idx = [np.where((risk.index >= b - pd.Timedelta(days=1)) & (risk.index <= b))[0] for b in risk.index[y == 1]]

def cv_predict(cols):
    p = np.zeros(n_days)
    Xa = risk[cols].values
    for wy in np.unique(years):
        tr, te = years != wy, years == wy
        mu, sd = Xa[tr].mean(0), Xa[tr].std(0) + 1e-12
        m = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, max_iter=5000).fit((Xa[tr] - mu) / sd, y[tr])
        p[te] = m.predict_proba((Xa[te] - mu) / sd)[:, 1]
    return p

def score(p):
    hits = sum(p[ix].max() >= 0.5 for ix in ev_idx)
    return dict(cv_logloss=log_loss(y, np.clip(p, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)), cv_brier=brier_score_loss(y, p),
                cv_AUC=roc_auc_score(y, p), cv_PR_AUC=average_precision_score(y, p),
                caught_p50=int(hits), false_alarm_days_p50=int(((p >= 0.5) & ~near).sum()))

res = []
for k in range(1, 5):
    for cols in itertools.combinations(CANDS, k):
        cols = list(cols)
        m = fit_logit(risk, cols)
        res.append(dict(inputs=" + ".join(cols), k=k, AIC=m.aic, BIC=m.bic, **score(cv_predict(cols))))
res = pd.DataFrame(res).sort_values("cv_logloss").reset_index(drop=True)

The selected linear model, examined

Code 
SEL = top.inputs.split(" + ")
msel = fit_logit(risk, SEL)
Xsel = pd.DataFrame(msel.model.exog, columns=msel.model.exog_names)
mclu = sm.Logit(y, Xsel).fit(disp=0, cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": risk.water_year.values})

def firth(Xm, yv, iters=200):
    """Firth's penalized likelihood: reduces small-sample bias when events are few."""
    b = np.zeros(Xm.shape[1])
    for _ in range(iters):
        p = expit(Xm @ b); W = p * (1 - p)
        inv = np.linalg.inv(Xm.T @ (Xm * W[:, None]))
        Xw = Xm * np.sqrt(W)[:, None]
        h = np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", Xw, inv, Xw)
        step = inv @ (Xm.T @ (yv - p + h * (0.5 - p)))
        b += step
        if np.abs(step).max() < 1e-9: break
    return b

bf = pd.Series(firth(msel.model.exog, y), index=msel.model.exog_names)
tab = pd.DataFrame({"coef (per SD)": msel.params, "SE": msel.bse, "SE clustered by water year": mclu.bse,
                    "p (clustered)": mclu.pvalues, "odds ratio": np.exp(msel.params),
                    "OR 95% CI low": np.exp(mclu.conf_int()[0]), "OR 95% CI high": np.exp(mclu.conf_int()[1]),
                    "Firth coef": bf})

Calibration and discrimination (held-out predictions)

Code 
psel = cv_predict(SEL)
def hosmer_lemeshow(yv, p, g=10):
    q = pd.qcut(p, g, duplicates="drop")
    t = pd.DataFrame({"y": yv, "p": p, "g": q}).groupby("g", observed=True).agg(o=("y", "sum"), e=("p", "sum"), n=("y", "size"))
    chi = (((t.o - t.e) ** 2) / (t.e * (1 - t.e / t.n) + 1e-12)).sum()
    return chi, stats.chi2.sf(chi, len(t) - 2)

hl_sel, hlp_sel = hosmer_lemeshow(y, psel)
hl_u, hlp_u = hosmer_lemeshow(y, pu)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.5, 3.8))
bins = np.r_[0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0001]
for p, lab in [(psel, "selected linear"), (pu, "website model")]:
    b = np.digitize(p, bins) - 1
    obs = [y[b == i].mean() if (b == i).any() else np.nan for i in range(len(bins) - 1)]
    pred = [p[b == i].mean() if (b == i).any() else np.nan for i in range(len(bins) - 1)]
    axs[0].plot(pred, obs, "o-", label=lab)
    f, t, _ = roc_curve(y, p); axs[1].plot(f, t, label=f"{lab} (AUC {roc_auc_score(y, p):.3f})")
axs[0].plot([0, 1], [0, 1], ":", color="gray"); axs[0].set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=0.01); axs[0].set_yscale("symlog", linthresh=0.01)
axs[0].set_xlabel("predicted daily chance"); axs[0].set_ylabel("observed breach rate"); axs[0].legend(fontsize=8); axs[0].set_title("Calibration")
axs[1].plot([0, 1], [0, 1], ":", color="gray"); axs[1].set_xlabel("false positive rate"); axs[1].set_ylabel("true positive rate")
axs[1].legend(fontsize=8); axs[1].set_title("ROC (held-out)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
md(f"Hosmer–Lemeshow on held-out predictions: selected model χ² = {hl_sel:.1f} (p = {hlp_sel:.3f}); "

Influence, residual dependence, and stability

Code 
glm = sm.GLM(y, msel.model.exog, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit()
cook = pd.Series(glm.get_influence().cooks_distance[0], index=risk.index)
top_inf = risk.assign(cooks_d=cook, p_fit=glm.fittedvalues).sort_values("cooks_d", ascending=False).head(6)
lb = acorr_ljungbox(glm.resid_pearson, lags=[1, 7], return_df=True)

Part 2. How the slough responds to rain

Storm events

A storm starts on a day with at least 0.1 in of rain after two dry days and continues while rain keeps falling (one-day gaps allowed). Storms of at least 0.25 in qualify when the mouth stayed closed from the day before through three days after, and a logger or the live sensor measured the level on at least 80% of those days. The response is the rise: the highest daily-mean level from the start of the storm to three days after it ends, minus the level the day before.

Code 
D = d.copy()
meas = D.stage_mean_ft.where(D.stage_src.fillna("").str.endswith(("_logger", "_sensor")))
r = D.rain_in.fillna(0); idx = D.index; n = len(D)
rows, t = [], 0
while t < n:
    if r.iloc[t] >= 0.1 and r.iloc[max(0, t - 2):t].sum() < 0.05:
        s = e = t
        while e + 1 < n and (r.iloc[e + 1] >= 0.05 or (e + 2 < n and r.iloc[e + 2] >= 0.05)): e += 1
        w0, w1 = idx[s] - pd.Timedelta(days=1), idx[e] + pd.Timedelta(days=3)
        win = D.loc[w0:w1]; tot = r.iloc[s:e + 1].sum()
        if tot >= 0.25 and (win.mouth == "closed").all() and meas.loc[w0:w1].notna().mean() >= 0.8 and pd.notna(meas.get(w0)):
            rows.append(dict(start=idx[s], total=tot, max_day=r.iloc[s:e + 1].max(), duration=e - s + 1,
                             api0=D.api.get(w0), rain_wy0=D.rain_wy.get(w0), stage0=meas[w0],
                             log_dc=np.log(D.days_closed.get(w0)), rise=meas.loc[idx[s]:w1].max() - meas[w0]))
        t = e + 1
    else:
        t += 1

def loo_rmse(formula, df):
    errs = []
    for i in range(len(df)):
        m = smf.ols(formula, df.drop(df.index[i])).fit()
        pred = m.predict(df.iloc[[i]]).iloc[0]
        if formula.startswith("np.log"): pred = np.exp(pred) - 0.05
        errs.append(df.rise.iloc[i] - pred)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(errs))))
rows = []

    m = smf.ols(f, E).fit()
    log_y = f.startswith("np.log")
    rows.append(dict(model=name, k=int(m.df_model), R2=m.rsquared, adj_R2=m.rsquared_adj,
                     AIC=np.nan if log_y else m.aic, BIC=np.nan if log_y else m.bic, LOO_RMSE_ft=loo_rmse(f, E)))

Daily distributed-lag model

The storm model rests on fewer than 30 events. Every closed-mouth day with a measured level adds far more data: the day’s change in level, regressed on that day’s and earlier days’ rain, rain above a threshold (bigger storms shed proportionally more runoff), and a seasonal evaporation term. Newey–West standard errors allow for day-to-day correlation.

Code 
L = D.copy()
L["meas"] = meas
L["dS"] = L.meas.diff()
L["closed2"] = (L.mouth == "closed") & (L.mouth.shift(1) == "closed")
for k in range(0, 5):
    L[f"P{k}"] = r.shift(k)
L["hinge"] = np.maximum(r - 0.5, 0)
L["season"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * (L.index.dayofyear - 200) / 365.25)
Ld = L[L.closed2 & L.dS.notna() & L.P4.notna() & (L.dS.abs() < 3)]  # > 3 ft/day while closed = logger glitch
rows, fits = [], {}
for nl in range(1, 6):
    f = "dS ~ " + " + ".join(f"P{k}" for k in range(nl)) + " + hinge + season"
    m = smf.ols(f, Ld).fit(cov_type="HAC", cov_kwds={"maxlags": 7})
    fits[nl] = m
    rows.append(dict(lags=f"0 to {nl - 1}", n_days=int(m.nobs), adj_R2=m.rsquared_adj, AIC=m.aic, BIC=m.bic,
                     ft_per_inch_lag_sum=sum(m.params[f"P{k}"] for k in range(nl)), hinge_ft_per_inch=m.params["hinge"]))
LG = pd.DataFrame(rows)
best_nl = int(LG.BIC.idxmin()) + 1
mb = fits[best_nl]
wald = mb.t_test(" + ".join(f"P{k}" for k in range(best_nl)) + " = 0")
ci = np.asarray(wald.conf_int())[0]
md(f"BIC selects rain lags 0 to {best_nl - 1}. Combined rise per inch of rain (sum of the lag coefficients): "
   f"**{float(np.asarray(wald.effect)[0]):.2f} ft per inch** (95% CI {ci[0]:.2f} to {ci[1]:.2f}), plus "
   f"**{mb.params['hinge']:.2f} ft** for each inch of a single day's rain above 0.5 in.")
display(LG.round(4))
pd.DataFrame({"coef": mb.params, "SE (Newey–West)": mb.bse, "p": mb.pvalues}).round(4)

Part 3. First breach of the season versus later ones

The held-out predictions in Part 1 split cleanly by event type. The first breach of a water year comes after months behind a tall, wave-built berm; any later breach that season comes days or weeks after the mouth closed again, behind a thin, young berm. If those behave differently, a model that knows which kind of berm it is facing should do better. Here later = 1 on closed-mouth days after the season’s first breach.

Code 
from scipy.special import expit
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from unified import Unified

wy_of = lambda t: t.year + (t.month >= 10)
bd_all = d.index[d.breach == 1]
bd_wy = np.array([wy_of(b) for b in bd_all])
risk["later"] = [int(((bd_all < t) & (bd_wy == wy_of(t))).any()) for t in risk.index]
risk["later_stage"] = risk.later * risk.stage
# crest floor, as in src/unified.py (highest level in the first 3 days after closing, known from then on)
closed = d.mouth.eq("closed")
spell = (closed & ~closed.shift(1, fill_value=False)).cumsum().where(closed)
early = d.stage_est.where(closed & (d.days_closed <= 3))
risk["crest_floor"] = early.groupby(spell).cummax().groupby(spell).ffill().shift(1).reindex(risk.index)
ev_dates = risk.index[y == 1]
ev_later = risk.later.values[y == 1]
evt = risk.loc[ev_dates, ["stage", "dc", "rain_in", "rain_3d", "rain_wy"]].assign(kind=np.where(ev_later, "later", "first"))

   f"{abs(evt.groupby('kind').stage.mean().diff().iloc[-1]):.1f} ft lower on average (Mann–Whitney p = {mw.pvalue:.4f}), "
   f"after a median of {evt[evt.kind == 'later'].dc.median():.0f} days closed versus {evt[evt.kind == 'first'].dc.median():.0f}. "
   f"`later` and log berm age correlate at r = {np.corrcoef(risk.later, risk.log_dc)[0, 1]:.2f} across all closed days.")
evt.groupby("kind").agg(["mean", "min", "max"]).round(2)

Candidate models

Same held-out scoring as Part 1, with catches split by event type. The website model is scored three ways: as shipped, refit here, and refit with one extra parameter that lowers (or raises) the crest for later berms on top of what berm age already does.

Code 
class UnifiedFL(Unified):
    names = Unified.names + ["d_later"]
    x0 = np.r_[Unified.x0, -1.5]
    def z(self, X, p=None):
        p = self.p if p is None else p
        crest = np.maximum(self.crest(X.dc, p), X.crest_floor.fillna(-np.inf)) + p[8] * X.later
        return p[3] + p[4] * (X.stage - crest) + p[5] * X.rain_in + p[6] * X.rain_3d + p[7] * X.api
    def fit(self, X, yv):
        yv = np.asarray(yv)
        def nll(p):
            pr = np.clip(expit(self.z(X, p)), 1e-9, 1 - 1e-9)
            prior = ((p[0] - 9.8) / 1.0) ** 2 / 2 + ((p[1] - 6.5) / 1.5) ** 2 / 2 + ((p[2] - np.log(70)) / 1.0) ** 2 / 2 \
                + 0.05 * np.sum(p[4:8] ** 2) + (p[8] / 1.5) ** 2 / 2
            return -np.sum(yv * np.log(pr) + (1 - yv) * np.log(1 - pr)) + prior
        best = None
        for start in (self.x0, self.x0 * [1, 1, 1, 1.5, 0.5, 2, 1, 1, 0.5]):
            r = minimize(nll, start, method="Nelder-Mead", options=dict(maxiter=20000, maxfev=20000, xatol=1e-5, fatol=1e-7))
            r = minimize(nll, r.x, method="BFGS")
            if best is None or r.fun < best.fun:
                best = r
        self.p = best.x
        return self

def cv_unified(cls):
    p = np.zeros(n_days)
    for wy in np.unique(years):
        tr, te = years != wy, years == wy
        p[te] = cls().fit(risk[tr], y[tr]).prob(risk[te])
    return p

def score_fl(p):
    out = score(p)
    hit = np.array([p[ix].max() >= 0.5 for ix in ev_idx])
    hl, hlp = hosmer_lemeshow(y, p)
    out.update(first_caught=f"{hit[ev_later == 0].sum()}/{(ev_later == 0).sum()}",
               later_caught=f"{hit[ev_later == 1].sum()}/{(ev_later == 1).sum()}", HL_p=hlp)
    return out

B3, B4 = ["rain_in", "rain_wy", "stage"], ["rain_in", "rain_3d", "rain_wy", "stage"]
FLP = {
    "website model, as shipped": pu,
    "website model, refit": cv_unified(Unified),
    "website model + later-berm crest shift": cv_unified(UnifiedFL),
    "3 inputs (rain_in + rain_wy + stage)": cv_predict(B3),
    "3 inputs + later": cv_predict(B3 + ["later"]),
    "3 inputs + later + later x stage": cv_predict(B3 + ["later", "later_stage"]),
    "best linear (rain_in + rain_3d + rain_wy + stage)": cv_predict(B4),
    "best linear + later": cv_predict(B4 + ["later"]),
    "best linear + later + later x stage": cv_predict(B4 + ["later", "later_stage"]),
}
FL = pd.DataFrame([dict(model=k, **score_fl(v)) for k, v in FLP.items()])
FL[["model", "cv_logloss", "cv_brier", "cv_AUC", "caught_p50", "first_caught", "later_caught", "false_alarm_days_p50", "HL_p"]].round(

Is the term real?

Code 
rows = []
for name, cols in (("3 inputs", B3), ("best linear", B4)):
    m0, m1, m2 = fit_logit(risk, cols), fit_logit(risk, cols + ["later"]), fit_logit(risk, cols + ["later", "later_stage"])
    rows.append(dict(base=name, later_coef_per_SD=m1.params["later"], LR_p_later=stats.chi2.sf(2 * (m1.llf - m0.llf), 1),
                     LR_p_interaction=stats.chi2.sf(2 * (m2.llf - m1.llf), 1)))
u0 = Unified().fit(risk, y); u1 = UnifiedFL().fit(risk, y)
nll_ = lambda m: -np.sum(y * np.log(np.clip(m.prob(risk), 1e-9, 1)) + (1 - y) * np.log(np.clip(1 - m.prob(risk), 1e-9, 1)))
p_shift = stats.chi2.sf(2 * (nll_(u0) - nll_(u1)), 1)
# season-block bootstrap of the later coefficient in the 3-input model
rng = np.random.default_rng(3); wys = np.unique(years); bl = []
for _ in range(400):
    idx = np.concatenate([np.where(years == w)[0] for w in rng.choice(wys, len(wys), replace=True)])
    sub = risk.iloc[idx]
    if sub.breach.sum() < 3 or sub.later.nunique() < 2 or sub.breach[sub.later == 1].sum() == 0:
        continue
    try:
        bb = fit_logit(sub, B3 + ["later"]).params["later"]
        if np.isfinite(bb) and abs(bb) < 50: bl.append(bb)
    except Exception:
        pass
bl = np.array(bl)
md(f"In the crest-curve model the extra shift fits at **{u1.p[8]:+.2f} ft** (likelihood-ratio p = {p_shift:.2f}): once berm age "
   f"is in the crest curve, knowing the berm is a later one adds nothing. In the linear models, which have no berm age, "
   f"`later` is strongly significant, and its sign is positive in {(bl > 0).mean():.0%} of {len(bl)} season-block bootstrap resamples.")
pd.DataFrame(rows).round(4)

In the crest-curve model the extra shift fits at -0.19 ft (likelihood-ratio p = 0.87): once berm age is in the crest curve, knowing the berm is a later one adds nothing. In the linear models, which have no berm age, later is strongly significant, and its sign is positive in 97% of 398 season-block bootstrap resamples.

What it means

Code

- **Later breaches really are different:** they happen about {abs(evt.groupby('kind').stage.mean().diff().iloc[-1]):.1f} ft lower, behind berms
  only days or weeks old.
- **The crest-curve model already knows this,** through berm age: a separate later-berm shift fits at {u1.p[8]:+.2f} ft and is not
  significant (p = {p_shift:.2f}). With breaches dated by when the slough drained, it has the best held-out log loss
  ({f.loc['website model, refit', 'cv_logloss']:.4f}) and passes the calibration test.
- **At the alert line the 3-input + later model has fewer false alarms:** at 30% it flags {a30.loc[('3 inputs + later', '30%'), 'caught']} breaches
  with {a30.loc[('3 inputs + later', '30%'), 'false_alarm_days']} false-alarm day(s), versus {a30.loc[('website model, as shipped', '30%'), 'caught']}
  with {a30.loc[('website model, as shipped', '30%'), 'false_alarm_days']} for the crest curve. Both miss the same two later breaches
  ({a30.loc[('3 inputs + later', '30%'), 'missed']}), young berms that broke at low levels after moderate rain.
- **Its percentages are less trustworthy as odds** (it fails the calibration test), but with 14 breaches that test has little to
  stand on, and the site uses the chance as a ranking with a single alert line.
- **Next:** Part 4 refits on days with a measured level, which is how the site runs, and settles the inputs.
""")
  • Later breaches really are different: they happen about 2.8 ft lower, behind berms only days or weeks old.
  • The crest-curve model already knows this, through berm age: a separate later-berm shift fits at -0.19 ft and is not significant (p = 0.87). With breaches dated by when the slough drained, it has the best held-out log loss (0.0088) and passes the calibration test.
  • At the alert line the 3-input + later model has fewer false alarms: at 30% it flags 12/14 breaches with 0 false-alarm day(s), versus 11/14 with 4 for the crest curve. Both miss the same two later breaches (2024-03-07, 2025-03-13), young berms that broke at low levels after moderate rain.
  • Its percentages are less trustworthy as odds (it fails the calibration test), but with 14 breaches that test has little to stand on, and the site uses the chance as a ranking with a single alert line.
  • Next: Part 4 refits on days with a measured level, which is how the site runs, and settles the inputs.

Part 4. Days with a measured level

The site always starts from a measured level: yesterday’s mean from the live sensor. Earlier seasons sometimes had no logger running, and on those days the level above is a staff-gauge reading rolled forward with rain, or a filled-in typical value. Here the models are refit and scored only on closed-mouth days whose level was measured the day before. Breaches on days without one are left out rather than counted as misses. Season-to-date rain is dropped (its coefficient was not significant), and rain the day before is tested as a lag term.

Code 
meas = d.stage_mean_ft.where(d.stage_src.fillna("").str.endswith(("_logger", "_sensor")))
risk["measured"] = meas.shift(1).reindex(risk.index).notna()
risk["rain_prev"] = d.rain_in.fillna(0).shift(1).reindex(risk.index)
M = risk[risk.measured].copy()
yM = M.breach.values
excluded = [str(b.date()) for b in risk.index[(risk.breach == 1) & ~risk.measured]]
evM = M.index[yM == 1]
ixM = [np.where((M.index >= b - pd.Timedelta(days=1)) & (M.index <= b))[0] for b in evM]
nearM = near[risk.measured.values]

def cvM(cols):
    p = np.zeros(len(M)); Xa = M[cols].values.astype(float); yrs = M.water_year.values
    for wy in np.unique(yrs):
        tr, te = yrs != wy, yrs == wy
        mu, sd = Xa[tr].mean(0), Xa[tr].std(0) + 1e-12
        m = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, max_iter=10000).fit((Xa[tr] - mu) / sd, yM[tr])
        p[te] = m.predict_proba((Xa[te] - mu) / sd)[:, 1]
    return p

def atM(p, thr):
    hit = np.array([p[ix].max() >= thr for ix in ixM])
    return dict(caught=f"{hit.sum()}/{len(hit)}", missed=", ".join(str(b.date()) for b, h in zip(evM, hit) if not h),
                false_alarm_days=int(((p >= thr) & ~nearM).sum()))

Part 5. Catching every breach

The goal for alerts is to flag every breach on the measured-level record with as few false alarms as possible; there is no fixed cutoff. For each model the cutoff is set as low as the weakest breach requires (its highest score on the breach day or the day before), and false alarms are counted at that cutoff, as days and as episodes (one alert per episode). That cutoff is tuned on the same predictions it is scored on, so each model is also checked honestly: every season’s cutoff comes only from the other seasons’ breaches. Every combination of up to five rain, level and berm-age inputs is searched; tide, surge and wave inputs are left out (they do not drive breaches here), and the crest-curve model is scored alongside.

Code 
C5 = ["rain_in", "rain_prev", "rain_3d", "api", "rain_wy", "log_dc", "stage", "later"]
X5 = M[C5].astype(float).fillna(M[C5].median()).values
yrsM = M.water_year.values
evyr = np.array([yrsM[ix[-1]] for ix in ixM])
def n_eps(idx): return int((np.diff(np.r_[-99, idx]) > 3).sum()) if len(idx) else 0
def catch_all(p, name):
    peaks = np.array([p[ix].max() for ix in ixM]); thr = peaks.min()
    fa = np.where((p >= thr) & ~nearM)[0]
    c, nfa, miss = 0, [], []
    for w in np.unique(yrsM):
        t = peaks[evyr != w].min()
        hit = peaks[evyr == w] >= t
        c += int(hit.sum()); miss += [str(evM[i].date()) for i in np.where(evyr == w)[0][~hit]]
        nfa += list(np.where((p >= t) & ~nearM & (yrsM == w))[0])
    return dict(model=name, cutoff=thr, fa_days=len(fa), fa_episodes=n_eps(fa), honest_caught=f"{c}/{len(peaks)}",
                honest_fa_days=len(nfa), honest_fa_episodes=n_eps(np.sort(nfa)), honest_missed=", ".join(miss),
                caught_50=int((peaks >= 0.5).sum()), fa_days_50=int(((p >= 0.5) & ~nearM).sum()))
rows5 = []
for k in range(1, 6):
    for cols in itertools.combinations(range(len(C5)), k):
        Xa = X5[:, cols]; p = np.zeros(len(M))
        for w in np.unique(yrsM):
            tr, te = yrsM != w, yrsM == w
            mu, sd = Xa[tr].mean(0), Xa[tr].std(0) + 1e-12
            p[te] = LogisticRegression(penalty=None, max_iter=5000).fit((Xa[tr] - mu) / sd, yM[tr]).predict_proba((Xa[te] - mu) / sd)[:, 1]
        rows5.append(catch_all(p, " + ".join(C5[c] for c in cols)))
pcrest = pu[risk.measured.values]
rows5.append(catch_all(pcrest, "crest curve (level vs rebuilding berm + rain_in + rain_3d + api)"))
R5 = pd.DataFrame(rows5)

R5.sort_values(["honest_caught", "honest_fa_episodes", "honest_fa_days"], ascending=[False, True, True]).head(10).round({"cutoff": 4})

Breach. Among 385 logistic models with up to four inputs, the best held-out performance came from rain_in + rain_3d + log_dc + stage: held-out log loss 0.0091 versus 0.0341 for a constant rate, with 11 of 14 breaches caught at 50% and 1 false-alarm days. The website’s model (nonlinear crest curve plus rain) scores 0.0085 and catches 11 of 14 with 3 false-alarm days. Tide height, surge and waves do not appear in the best model. With 14 events, differences of a few thousandths in log loss are within noise; the events-per-variable limit and the bootstrap sign stability are the guardrails.

Slough rise. Across 28 storms the best leave-one-storm-out model was rise ~ total + stage0 (error 0.35 ft, versus 0.70 ft for the mean alone). The daily distributed-lag model, using 2,219 closed-mouth days, puts the response at 0.51 ft per inch of rain spread over 3 day(s), plus 0.31 ft per inch of a single day’s rain above 0.5 in.
